__dayInLife: On a cross-functional team, your day is about steering a product: what to build, why, and how it wins. You carry out the strategic and planning work: shaping product vision and go-to-market strategy, defining feature vision and scope, framing problems, setting priorities and the roadmap, running kickoff and sprint planning, researching the market, and positioning the product. Because product management wears many hats, you are accountable for a very wide span of delivery, from requirements, design, and QA through architecture and launch, making sure the whole thing adds up to something users want and the business can sustain. You are consulted across nearly every part of the team. A typical day mixes strategy and planning in Notion, Trello, and FigJam with heavy collaboration: standups, stakeholder alignment, backlog refinement, and working sessions with design, research, and engineering. You steer in short loops, adjust as the market and users teach you, and keep everyone pointed at the highest-value work.

Academia.gaps: As a product manager you are responsible for product vision, strategy, priorities, and the roadmap, and you are accountable across the whole delivery, from requirements and design through QA and launch. Academia gave you deep analysis, the ability to frame big questions, and strong writing, which help you shape vision and reason about a market. Research Analysis and Problem-Solving transfer. What is new is the business and go-to-market side, product-market fit, positioning, and pricing, plus the agile machinery for steering delivery, worked in Notion, Trello, and FigJam.
Academia.training: Start with Vision Formation and Backlog Management, then add Go-to-Market Strategy and Product-Market Fit, the business muscles academia does not build. Practice turning a big idea into a vision, a roadmap, and prioritized work. Because you are accountable across delivery, learn enough of requirements, design, and QA to steer the whole. Pick up Notion and Trello, and learn Scrum. Lean on your analysis while the market and agile sense grow.
